title: Side section of the hall
what: A cut through the stage house and the stalls: a fly loft with ropes, flats and trusses seen end-on, the followspot hanging over the stage, the deck with its understage frame, a pit, and raked rows of seated people with a balcony above, all in architectural hatching.
why: A section shows the whole machine at once: what is paid for above the stage (rigging, truss, lamp) and who it is paid for (the rows watching). The spot lands on one board of the deck; the hatching and sightline make it feel like a plan someone really signed off.
how: Section drawing with 45 degree hatching for walls, slabs and the rake (clipped by clip paths), people drawn in profile, seats as small L shapes. The pointer anywhere over the drawing slides the spot along the stage and the lamp turns; the beam is a thin cone to a flat pool. Draw-in on entry, static under reduced motion, same scaling on mobile.
